Video Description (Original):
Here is a question that was asked  of me recently: “Do you believe in Jesus?”

It was beyond my capacity to explain to this young man the obtuse nature of that question. And all my attempts to describe the depths that I have discovered in Christ fell on deaf ears.

The question is a coded pledge of allegiance to the status quo. The demand for a positive response to that question is less than love. It is the same inquisition that the Protestants say they despise in catholic history. It is the lynching of the women we called witches. It is the crushing of the indigenous people and the erasing of their languages and cultures. It is the importation of human beings to pick our cotton, the building of a nation on the backs of enslaved humanity.

This is common knowledge now: the enslavement never ended. 

Now what will we do about it?
When I was twenty-seven years old I became a police officer. After one year, what I discovered was this: I could not be the hand of a justice system that is so often unjust…

We are all trying to survive in this man-made jungle of commercial materialism. Humans crafted clothing, shelter, and finally the assembly line to increase our comfort. The resulting death-machine demands nothing less than our very souls. 

Returning to Spirit time and time again, we finally understand this: God wants to deliver us from our sick and dying culture. 

Participation in sick culture only leads to continued sickness.
What the doctors are trained to label as pathology in an individual, is actually the increasing symptoms of our ailing species. Big Pharma has no interest in a cure. We are now only suppressing the symptoms of our shared neurosis.

When we resist with hate and anger we only give strength to that which would crush us. We must create alternate culture. Love-Centered Community in all forms is our last form of resistance.

Transcending Abuse:

I wrote protest songs for a while.

This song is nearly 20 years old. 

It was born from a painful breakup with a church family and a first hand disillusionment of our justice system.

Jesus showed us how to release the personal. This is what it means to become the Christ: Christ transcends the personal (non-attachment = non-personal = Forgiveness) Jesus was not attached to his body, or his name, or his emotions or his thoughts. This is the freedom that he came to share with us. This is what it means to be the One. You are also the One, when you are ready to be.

When forgiveness seems impossible, it is because we are attached to ourselves. We are taking things personally. Egos never forgive because true forgiveness is death of the ego.

Jesus knew that his crucifixion was not personal. He was living among the unconscious (fearful). In becoming the Christ (the One who does not take things personally, the One who forgives) he invited us to make that journey also.

Many of us had abusive parents. And the church often behaves much like abusive parents (especially for those of us who learned to play the victim as a child). As victims, we unconsciously ask for abuse. We must educate ourselves to escape these sick cycles.

I encountered a church that was barely capable to help me, so they had to crucify me. I forgive them, they had no idea what they were doing, and neither did I. 

the current iterations of our churches, families, and justice system gives us great opportunity to forgive.

we must not shut our mouths in shame about these abuses. No. In fact, these are exactly the things that we need to learn to talk about, however difficult a journey that may become. As we gain enough courage to address these issues, we are actively freeing ourselves. 

Families, churches, and governments are all deeply affected by these unaddressed neuroses. Some of us who are attached to false ideas about church, family, and government, may not want to hear about these abuses. That is understandable, but we must persist, for the liberation of us all. We must learn to speak with confidence and precision about these things.

When we learn to talk about the abuse, with forgiveness in our hearts, a light is shined on it. We become honest with ourselves and the ones we love. We can recover.

As my parents passed their trauma down to me, I have also passed down that trauma to my children, and my students, and everyone I have ever been close to. It is unfortunate, but necessary to work with.

It is important that we come to understand ourselves in this way, as part of an unfolding depth of consciousness that we call Love. When we see from this cosmic (Christ) perspective we are no longer obligated to take anything personally.

God help us
Letting go of what we once knew takes a faith beyond superstition. It takes a hope that fills us with a hunger, that may never be satisfied.

These chord changes to Stella By Starlight have continued to speak to me for years.

I had the great privilege of being part of a Jazz community at UCO back in the 90s.

Thank God for all those teachers who saw potential in me and invited me in to learn and grow through the devoted study of music.

May we all find our communities where we can become the teachers and students that our world so deeply needs.

All areas of my work keep returning to the same solution.

Search for 12
Be in a Band

A band represents to me our lost tribal nature. By “tribal nature” I am referring to the communities from which humanity evolved. I am referring to the mind that was not yet enslaved to the separate-self.

There was once an organismic consciousness in our communal connection to being. We lost that sense of organism when we civilized ourselves, believing ourselves to be separate from nature (centralized government means surrender of Self-governance).

I am not suggesting that we can regress to a former state of evolution. But I am suggesting that we may be able to integrate a wisdom from our deep past.

I can see this organismal wisdom as I review the spark of life that I experienced as I learned music in communities. In bands, we are aligning ourselves with harmonic and rhythmic patterns, syncing our frequencies.

Humanity needs more of this practice now.

Video Description (Original):
I do not wish to be supported by the government. Yet, I have a neurodivergency (a calling) that does not allow me to participate in the traditional work force. These videos represent my search for a solution. I am reaching out to those of you who are also searching for alternate ways of surviving and thriving in this world. 

Humans evolved as functioning tribal organisms. Our current work systems have alienated us from our deeper nature. Some of us (Neurodivergents/X-men) feel this alienation more than others. 

When I choose to pathologize my experience by attaching to a mental health diagnosis there are many negative consequences. Viewing my experience through the lens of pathology does not bring sufficient sight. 

Being unable to participate in paid-work activities is not necessarily a symptom of mental illness. I am very capable. I am working very hard. I am donating my time and services. But, I have much difficulty monetizing my work.

My brother’s suicide prompted me to dive deeper into the healing of our generational trauma.

My brother died because he believed that he was completely exhausted. And he believed that he was alone.

Trauma convinces us that we are separated. Incapable of truly connecting with others, we wither and die. 

Humanity was not born of isolated individuals, or even isolated nuclear families. Our species was born of a high functioning communal mind. We are an organismic being, all of us. We are generous and nurturing. This is the culture from which we arose.

We are returning to our own deep-time nature, a fuller expression of our most loving Being.

When we help and individual to discover their depth, a tribe is deepened. Deeper tribes, in turn, bring the kingdom of heaven here to earth (where two or more are gathered…).

There is much work to do. Much education. Much to build. Much to discover. 

Thank you for joining me on this adventure.

Video Description (Original): Thanks to everyone who has contributed in all the various ways you have given to this life. Gratitude! Gratitude! Gratitude!

A few years ago I began accepting invitations from people who value my deepest work.

I had made a connection with a young man named Ian. Ian and I met as I was reaching the end of my work in Physical Therapy. The care that he received through me helped him to come into a healthier and more whole place, and all of his family recognized that he had made a turn.

Over the next years, we continued to reach out to one another. So, when Ian extended an invitation for me to join him and his friends as they worked construction in Key West, I accepted.

I was welcomed into a tribe. I was welcomed into the process that these young men were engaged in as they tried to help one another. I saw three men who were actively trying to impart to one another the wisdom that they each carried.

I saw three men who were bravely testing the limits of their capacity to help one another get to their next waypoint. And I was invited to participate.

The prayer in my heart as I made my way along the Southern coast that summer was for community.

I am truly grateful for those three men who shared their lives with me that summer in Key West as we were all trying to move forward into that next right action.

Video Description (Original):
While in Santa Fe, I had the honor of discussing some of the most painful human topics imaginable with Jazz Musician Delbert Anderson. Genocide, Colonization, Re-Education, Appropriation, Oppression, Marginalization, Racism

Appropriation is an especially charged topic among indigenous artists. Musical ideas pass freely among fellow musicians. But what happens when culture is hijacked by a ruling-class to serve its own purpose? 

“Tikkun Olam” is a Hebrew phrase which points to the Re-Pairing of the world. How do we heal our broken world when we all seem to be so broken ourselves?

How do we escape our roles as oppressed and oppressor? 

What does it mean to be marginalized? 

How does one come in to the big family? 

What kind of ceremonies might we have to pass through in order to see clearly and live strong? 

How do we rise up justly within an unjust system? 

How can we learn to listen and respect others in ways that promote the healing of our world?
